title: Abstract: The Art of Design | Platon: Photography
notes: A full episode following Platon’s portrait practice and his focus on simplicity, connection, and storytelling.

title: Annie Leibovitz Teaches Photography
notes: A MasterClass course on portraiture, developing concepts, working with subjects, natural light, and post-production.

title: Find Your Frame
notes: Useful for developing a personal way of seeing, composing, and anticipating moments on the street.

title: Finding Vivian Maier (2013)
notes: A documentary exploring Vivian Maier’s life and the discovery of her extensive photographic archive.

title: Fred Herzog: Modern Color
notes: A vivid survey of Fred Herzog’s pioneering color street photography and his distinctive view of mid-century Vancouver.

title: Jimmy Chin Teaches Adventure Photography
notes: A MasterClass course on planning, capturing, and editing adventure photography in demanding environments.

title: Light: Science & Magic
notes: A practical guide to understanding how light behaves and using it intentionally, with examples for solving photographic lighting challenges.

title: Magnum Contact Sheets
notes: A look at the frames behind iconic Magnum photographs, revealing how photographers work a scene and select their final images.

title: Making Candid Portraits in Street Photography (feat. Dawn Eagleton)
notes: A conversation with Dawn Eagleton about creating candid street portraits and capturing authentic, unguarded moments.

title: PetaPixel
notes: A great photography news and review site for keeping up with new gear and the industry.

title: PhotoPills
notes: A photography planning app for predicting the position of the Sun, Moon, and Milky Way, scouting locations, and calculating technical details before a shoot.

title: Saul Leiter: The Centennial Retrospective
notes: A wide-ranging retrospective of Saul Leiter’s color, black-and-white, fashion, and painted work.

title: Tales by Light
notes: This Netflix documentary series follows photographers and filmmakers as they travel the world, capturing indelible images of people, places, creatures, and cultures.

title: The Candid Frame
notes: Ibarionex Perello’s conversations with photographers about their creative lives, personal journeys, and approaches to making images.

title: The Creative Act: A Way of Being — Rick Rubin
notes: An excellent book with so many insights into creativity. While it is not a photography book, its ideas apply to photography and building a creative life.

title: The Creative Thread
notes: Hosted by photographer Meg Loeks, The Creative Thread is a podcast about art, process, and the stories behind the work.

title: The Defenders: Heroes of the Fight for Global Human Rights
notes: Platon’s powerful portraits and photo essays document people fighting for human rights around the world.

title: The Meaning in the Making — Sean Tucker
notes: Explores why we create and how to build a meaningful creative practice, with ideas that reach beyond photography.

title: The PetaPixel Podcast
notes: A weekly panel discussion of photography news and gear from the PetaPixel team.

title: The Photographer’s Eye — Michael Freeman
notes: Useful for developing an eye for composition and organizing the visual elements of a scene into stronger photographs.

title: Think Like a Street Photographer
notes: Useful for developing a more observant, patient, and playful approach to street photography.

title: Through the Glass
notes: Dawn Eagleton’s candid street portraits use windows, reflections, and layers to find intimate moments in everyday life.

title: Understanding Color in Photography
notes: Useful for thinking intentionally about color, composition, and exposure when creating vivid photographs.

title: Vivian Maier: The Color Work
notes: A revealing collection of Vivian Maier’s color photographs that expands the familiar view of her street photography.

title: Walkie Talkie — Paulie B
notes: A video series following street photographers on photo walks, sharing conversations about their approach, process, and ways of seeing.

title: Stunna Photo Tools
notes: Free browser photo filters, photo booth frames and a photo strip maker for trying film and digicam looks on existing photos. Images are processed locally; no account or watermark, with 20 MB inputs and exports up to 3000 px. Owner-submitted; the site also promotes a separate mobile AI editor with optional paid Pro access.
